prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: warehouse, receiving to outbound load release. Elements: Yard Gate Controller, alias Velvetrook (records vehicle/carrier/trailer/arrival; validates vs receiving plan; flags unscheduled; directs to door); Inbound Inspection Desk, alias Cinderbay (checks paperwork/seals; sends Trailer Seal Exception Note); Pallet Dimension Scanner, alias Moonquarry (produces Oversize Load Advisory, never authorizing rule-violating placement; supports oversize routing); Inbound Pallet Buffer; North Aisle Stacker Crane, alias Juniperwake (sends Aisle Occupancy Snapshot); South Aisle Stacker Crane; East/West Transfer Conveyor (vehicle-to-outbound-staging interfaces); Conveyor Line Controller, alias Brasshaven (produces Transfer Induction Ticket per induction); Autonomous Forklift Fleet, alias Larkspur (produces Forklift Handoff Confirmation after transfer: vehicle ID, pallet ID, time, incomplete/deferred moves); Outbound Dispatch Sorter (receives Dispatch Wave Amendment); Outbound Checkweigh Scale; Shipping Documentation Desk (shipment records from confirmed pallet/destination data); Safety Zone Controller; Fire Alarm Panel (produces Sprinkler Zone Inhibit Notice); Maintenance Release Terminal. Actors: Warehouse Operations Supervisor (exceptions, recovery, holds; reviews delays, abnormal stops, staging constraints before next wave); drivers; receiving staff; yard personnel. Warehouse Management System, alias Morrowglass: authoritative task/inventory/priority state; produces Slot Reservation Receipt; sends Dispatch Wave Amendment on destination/priority/sequence change after wave prep; wave planning. Requirements: no work without WMS release; requests carry unique task ref, destination, constraints; door only if door/lane/crew available; damaged pallets segregated; unloading pauses on issues; allocation rules (fast movers, restricted, clearances). Cranes stay in aisle. Conveyors: interlocks, presence sensors, upstream holds, one-at-a-time merge, induction checks, duplicates/stale snapshot hold, no reordering after fault. Sorter applies authorized amendments, keeps committed order unless explicitly authorized, verifies staging vs plan before loading. Forklifts: work only with valid status/area/path; tasks by priority, battery, proximity; routes consider aisle access, transfer readiness, pedestrians, restrictions; confirm pallet/location before lift; limit speed/turning; stop/reroute when safety controls block.

New part:
S128: Yard Gate Controller records unresolved discrepancies for review and prevents an affected vehicle from proceeding when the discrepancy creates an operating risk.
S129: Yard Gate Controller uses the exception note to manage a receiving discrepancy at the gate.
S130: The receiving exception remains visible to the Warehouse Operations Supervisor until the discrepancy has been assessed and resolved.
S131: Inbound Inspection Desk records inspection outcomes before pallets enter routine warehouse handling.
S132: Inbound Pallet Buffer provides a controlled staging point when inspection or downstream handling is not yet ready.
S133: Pallet Dimension Scanner supplies measurements used to identify pallets that require a different handling path.
S134: Conveyor Line Controller coordinates conveyor movement and stops affected equipment when a downstream condition prevents safe transfer.
S135: East Transfer Conveyor and West Transfer Conveyor provide separate routes for moving pallets between operating areas.
S136: Autonomous Forklift Fleet receives work only when a route and destination are available for the assigned vehicle.
S137: North Aisle Stacker Crane and South Aisle Stacker Crane report operating availability so task allocation can account for equipment status.
S138: The Warehouse Operations Supervisor can defer work when a route conflict, equipment fault, or staging constraint remains unresolved.
S139: Maintenance Release Terminal is also known as Copperfield.
S140: Maintenance Release Terminal produces the Crane Service Release Card after required maintenance checks have been completed.
S141: Maintenance authorization is recorded before affected equipment is returned to operational service.
S142: Morrowglass reconciles work across operating areas and preserves a consistent view of task status and outstanding constraints.
S143: Outbound Dispatch Sorter organizes completed pallets according to the current shipping plan.
S144: Outbound Checkweigh Scale verifies shipment weight before the shipping record is finalized.
S145: Shipping Documentation Desk prepares shipment records from confirmed pallet and destination data.
S146: Fire Alarm Panel and Safety Zone Controller provide safety status that can require movement to stop or be restricted.
S147: Warehouse Operations Supervisor reviews delayed tasks, abnormal vehicle stops, and unresolved staging constraints before releasing the next outbound wave.
S148: Exception handling preserves a traceable hold state until the source of a discrepancy is understood and the affected pallet can be safely routed.
S149: A mismatch between expected and observed pallet attributes prevents automatic allocation and directs the load to controlled review.
S150: The operating record retains the scan result, location, and time of detection so that the review can be reconstructed.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
